newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq gives U.N. draft food plan, more talks seen.
newsitem.headline: Iraq gives U.N. draft food plan, more talks seen.

text.p: Iraq has given the United Nations a preliminary draft of its food procurement and distribution plan to cover the next six months of oil exports, Iraq's U.N. coordinator said on Wednesday.
"We have received last night from the government of Iraq a preliminary draft of the (food) distribution plan," Staffan de Mistura told Reuters.
He said the U.N. had no objection to Iraq resuming partial sales at any time. "It is an Iraqi condition to hold up sales until the completion of the distribution plan," he added.

De Mistura said he would hold further meetings with Iraqi officials to fill in the gaps in the draft he received on Tuesday. He did not say how serious these gaps were or how long the discussions would take.

Iraq's plan concerns the central and southern parts of the country. De Mistura said U.N. agencies had their plan for the three northern provinces of Dahouk, Arbil and Sulaimaniya, currently outside the control of the central government in Baghdad, ready since June 29.
The two plans have to be incorporated into a unified national programme before presenting them to the United Nations.
Iraq has held up partial exports pending the completion of its distribution plan. The U.N. Security Council renewed the limited oil sales deal on June 8.
"It is a good step in the right direction," de Mistura said, but added that Iraq's plan still needed to be worked on before submitting the draft to the U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan for approval.
"Some important sectors are still missing, hence we will need more discussions prior to its submission to the U.N. secretary general," de Mistura said.

Iraq first started limited exports in December last year and completed its $2 billion worth quota late in May. The U.N. has allowed Iraq partial sales to be able to satisfy urgent needs of its people labouring under U.N. trade sanctions imposed after its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
In the first six months Iraq earned about $1.3 billion, of which $260 million was earmarked for the northern provinces. Iraq is expected to receive a similar amount of money in the next six months.
More than one million tonnes of food from the first partial sales have arrived in Iraq so far but only small quantities of medical supplies have reached the country.
Iraq has repeatedly complained about the sluggish pace of approving contracts under the deal.
